newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Swedish debt/currency market closing report.
newsitem.headline: Swedish debt/currency market closing report.

text.p: Swedish debt yields ended down on Thursday, helped by the lower U.S. yields following U.S. second quarter GDP data. But dealers said they expected yields to rise on Friday.
After the Swedish close U.S. Treasuries were unchanged in volatile trade and German Bunds had slipped back. Dealers said they expected bears to emerge on Friday.
"Swedish yields will probably also rise tomorrow. Markets have performed well for a long time and you get to a point where people start profit-taking," one dealer said.
Next in focus are the U.S. unemployment figures on Friday.
Six-month T-bill rates fell one basis point to 4.28 percent and ten-year bond yields shed one basis point to 6.38 percent.
The crown firmed to 7.9684 against the weaker dollar from 7.9971 late on Wednesday. Against the mark the crown firmed to 4.3335 from 4.3385.
